questions.question: The MGFs of $X$ and $Y$ are finite and equal on an open interval around $0$. What follows?
options: Only that $X$ and $Y$ have the same mean

questions.question: $X$ and $Y$ have the same distribution, and their MGFs are finite on an open interval $I$ containing $0$. Which statement must hold?
Two random variables satisfy $M_X(0)=M_Y(0)$. What does this say about their distributions?
options: They have the same finite mean
They have the same finite variance

questions.question: The $\mathcal{N}(\mu,\sigma^2)$ MGF is $\mathrm{e}^{\mu t+\sigma^2t^2/2}$. A variable has $M_X(t)=\mathrm{e}^{-t+2t^2}$ near $0$. Which law does it have?
A variable has $M_X(t)=(0.7+0.3\,\mathrm{e}^t)^4$ for all $t$. Which law does it have?
Near $0$ a count has $M_X(t)=\exp(5(\mathrm{e}^t-1))$. What is $\mathbb{P}(X=0)$?
A waiting time has $M_X(t)=\dfrac4{4-t}$ for $t<4$, the form $\dfrac\lambda{\lambda-t}$ of an exponential law. What is $\mathbb{P}(X>1)$?
A variable has $M_X(t)=\tfrac14\mathrm{e}^{-t}+\tfrac34\mathrm{e}^{t}$ for all $t$. Which distribution is this?
options: A fair $\pm1$ coin: each value has probability $\tfrac12$
The values $\tfrac14$ and $\tfrac34$, each taken half of the time

questions.question: Which random variable has MGF $\mathrm{e}^{3t}$ for all $t$?
For $b>0$, $\operatorname{Unif}(0,b)$ has MGF $\dfrac{\mathrm{e}^{bt}-1}{bt}$ for $t\ne0$. A variable has $M_X(t)=\dfrac{\mathrm{e}^{2t}-1}{2t}$ for $t\ne0$. What is $\mathbb{P}(X<\tfrac12)$?

$X$ takes $-3$ and $3$ with probability $\tfrac12$ each. $Y$ takes $-6$, $0$ and $6$ with probabilities $\tfrac18$, $\tfrac34$ and $\tfrac18$. A student finds that both means are $0$ and both variances are $9$, then invokes MGF uniqueness to claim equal distributions. What is the error?
options: Uniqueness cannot be used for finite-support variables
Uniqueness requires independence of the two variables
Equal first two moments do not establish equal MGFs
An MGF must be finite for every real argument

questions.question: Two variables have equal finite moments of every order, but their MGFs are infinite for every $t>0$. Does the stated MGF uniqueness theorem establish that their distributions are equal?
options: Yes: equal moments guarantee equal MGFs near $0$
No: the required finite neighbourhood is missing
Yes: both MGFs have the same infinite values for $t>0$
Yes: both MGFs are finite and equal at $t=0$

questions.question: Let $X$ and $Y$ be independent normal variables and let $Z$ have the proposed normal law for their sum. A proof establishes $M_{X+Y}(t)=M_X(t)M_Y(t)=M_Z(t)$ for every real $t$. Which argument completes the proof that $X+Y$ and $Z$ have the same distribution?
options: Equality of the first derivatives at $0$ identifies the entire law
The product rule alone identifies the law of the sum
The common value $1$ at $0$ identifies the entire law
Finite MGF agreement around $0$ identifies the entire law

questions.question: A variable has $M_Y(t)=\mathrm{e}^{2t}\big(\tfrac12+\tfrac12\mathrm{e}^t\big)^3$ for all real $t$. What is $\mathbb{P}(Y=3)$?
The MGF $0.2+0.5\,\mathrm{e}^{t}+0.3\,\mathrm{e}^{3t}$, valid for all real $t$, belongs to a variable $X$. Given that $X$ is positive, how likely is it to be at most $2$?
A variable has $M_X(t)=\big(\dfrac3{3-t}\big)^2$ for $t<3$. Which variable has the same distribution as $X$?
options: The sum of two independent $\operatorname{Exp}(3)$ waiting times
The larger of two independent $\operatorname{Exp}(3)$ waiting times

questions.question: $M_X(s)$ is finite for $|s|<1/7$, and $M_Y(s)$ is finite for $|s|<1/11$. Whenever both sides are finite, $M_X(5t)=\mathrm{e}^{8t}M_Y(-3t)$. Write $U\stackrel{d}{=}V$ when $U$ and $V$ have the same distribution. Which common interval do these bounds certify, and which equality in distribution follows?

A variable has $M_X(t)=\tfrac15+\tfrac45\mathrm{e}^{6t+8t^2}$ near $0$. The MGF of $\mathcal{N}(\mu,\sigma^2)$ is $\mathrm{e}^{\mu t+\sigma^2t^2/2}$. What does MGF uniqueness let us conclude about the law of $X$?
options: The law is uniquely determined, with an atom at $0$ and a normal component
The law is uniquely determined and is purely continuous
The law is uniquely determined and is supported on $\{0,6\}$
The law is not uniquely determined because it combines two MGF terms

questions.question: A variable has $M_X(t)=\dfrac{\mathrm{e}^t}{2-\mathrm{e}^t}$ for $t<\ln2$. Expanding it as a geometric series in $\tfrac12\mathrm{e}^t$, what is $\mathbb{P}(X=3)$?

A variable has $M_X(t)=\mathrm{e}^{-3t}\exp\big(4(\mathrm{e}^{2t}-1)\big)$ for all real $t$. A Poisson variable with parameter $\lambda$ has MGF $\exp\big(\lambda(\mathrm{e}^t-1)\big)$. What is $\mathbb{P}(X<0)$?
